notes.summary: The actual quotient is a compact connected smooth complex threefold and an elliptic bundle over P1×P1. The descending Hermitian form satisfies dω≠0, d(ω²)=0, and ∫ω³=24π. Primary evidence for the allowed foundations was checked.
notes.detailedSummary: Constructs the quotient using the free properly discontinuous action and explicit bundle transition functions. Proves compactness, positivity, genuine nonclosedness, and the exact volume. Supplies the normalized strictly positive closed test ω²/(24π). Records the precise permitted foundation applications without claiming recursive certification of their cited dependencies.
notes.text:
This is an ordinary unverified proof draft for the named-factor dependency. The separately allowed foundations are the only imported non-elementary theorems. Original unrestricted P07 remains unresolved.

Write α=α0 and β=β0. The map π:Ω→P1×P1 sends [z:w] to ([z],[w]). On the base chart z_i w_j≠0, choose representatives with z_i=1 and put c=w_j/z_i∈C*. This gives π^{-1}(U_ij)≅U_ij×C*. On overlaps,
c_{i'j'}=c_{ij}(w_{j'}/w_j)/(z_{i'}/z_i).
These are actual holomorphic transition maps. The action of g is c↦qc, so quotient bundle charts are U_ij×(C*/q^Z). Their logarithmic fibre coordinate belongs to E=C/(2πZ+2πiZ). Logarithms of transition functions give translations in E independent of the chosen logarithm. On U_00 the coordinates are exactly x=z1/z0, y=w1/w0, ζ=log(w0/z0).

The action is free: [z:q^m w]=[z:w], with z,w≠0, forces the projective scalar to be 1 and then q^m=1. It is properly discontinuous because t(g^m P)=t(P)+4πm: compact subsets of Ω have bounded t and meet only finitely many translates. Small open sets with disjoint translates give quotient manifold charts. Thus X0 is a smooth complex threefold. Ω is connected as the image of (C²∖{0})×(C²∖{0}), hence X0 is connected. Every quotient point has a representative z=Z, w=e^{t/2}W with Z,W∈S³ and 0≤t≤4π. The image of this compact parameter set covers X0, proving compactness.

On U_00,
t=ζ+barζ+log(1+|y|²)−log(1+|x|²),
α=dd^c log(1+|x|²)=σ_x/(1+|x|²)²,
β=dd^c log(1+|y|²)=σ_y/(1+|y|²)².
Polar integration gives ∫P1α=∫P1β=1. Put s=α+β, F=β−α and ρ=dt∧d^c t. Then dd^c t=F and ρ=(i/(2π))∂t∧bar∂t≥0. Although t is not a real-valued function on X0, its derivatives are invariant under g. Therefore ω=s+ρ descends. The horizontal part is positive in the two base directions, and ∂t has nonzero vertical component dζ, making ω strictly positive.

Since dρ=−dt∧F, dω=−dt∧F≠0: evaluate on a vertical real direction with dt≠0 and an α-horizontal complex line. Moreover α²=β²=ρ²=0 and sF=0, so d(ω²)=−2s∧dt∧F=0. Direct differentiation gives dd^cρ=−F²=2αβ.

On a fibre write ζ=a+ib. Then dt=2da, d^c t=db/(2π), and ρ=da∧db/π=σ_ζ. Both a and b have period 2π, hence ∫Eρ=4π. Since ω³=6αβρ, fibre integration gives ∫X0ω³=24π. Consequently Θ*=ω²/(24π) is a globally smooth strictly positive CLOSED (2,2) form with ∫ωΘ*=1.

The exact foundation applications were checked at public primary sources. Tosatti–Weinkove, arXiv0910.1390v2, Corollary 1, printed p.1, supplies smooth Hermitian MA existence up to a scalar: https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390v2 . In n5 it applies to connected compact X0 of dimension 3, arbitrary smooth Hermitian h, and smooth positive volume η_j³. Its source potential is multiplied by 2π; no degeneration estimate is imported.

Lamari, AIF49(1999), Lemma 3.3, printed pp.275–276, supplies the criterion for a smooth (1,1) form without assuming closedness, using every smooth positive dd^c-closed test: https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1999__49_1_263_0.pdf . In n2 it is applied to ω−κBδ. Positive rescaling of the source operator leaves the test kernel and distributional potential range unchanged. Proposition 1.3 is unnecessary because Θ* explicitly proves nonemptiness.

Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, 21 June 2012, I.5.8–5.9, printed p.40, supplies canonical psh representatives and local L1 compactness. III.8.5, printed p.174, supplies analytic geometric Lelong upperlevel sets for positive CLOSED currents of bidimension (p,p): https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf . In n2 global normalized compactness is reconstructed, and Siu is applied only to locally closed positive corrections with p=2, never directly to ω+dd^c u.

notes.summary: Proves I against the entire normalized smooth positive dd^c-closed test family: Cδ is finite and tends to infinity for every allowed p and χ0. Includes genuine normalized compactness and the explicit divisor-accumulation contradiction.
notes.detailedSummary: A bounded subsequence of Cδ would, by Lamari, produce canonical ω-psh potentials whose corrected currents dominate a fixed multiple of Bδ. A submean propagation argument supplies global L1 compactness. Closed positive local corrections allow Siu's theorem, producing an analytic set containing ζ=0 locally. Its lift must contain every hyperplane w0=q^m z0. A power-series argument at [0:1:0:1] forces interior, contradicting dimension at most 2. No pairing estimate is inferred from local compactness alone.
notes.text:
Use the quotient geometry from n1. The prescribed Bδ is globally smooth after extension by zero: the base cutoffs are compactly supported, and the smooth density p vanishes with all derivatives at its support boundary. Its ζ-support lies in an injective logarithmic neighbourhood. It is semipositive. On a fixed compact neighbourhood of these supports, σ_ζ≤Kω, so
0≤Bδ≤K||p||∞δ^{-2}ω.
Every normalized positive test therefore satisfies ∫BδΘ≤K||p||∞δ^{-2}. Thus Cδ is finite. Its test family is nonempty by Θ* from n1.

We first reconstruct the compactness needed below. On a connected compact complex manifold, genuine quasi-psh functions u_j with dd^c u_j≥−h for fixed smooth Hermitian h and sup u_j=0 have an L1-convergent subsequence. Choose finitely many relatively compact connected coordinate balls, with smaller cores covering the manifold. On each choose a bounded quadratic correction ρ with dd^cρ≥h. Then u_j+ρ is genuine psh. Subtracting a fixed upper bound for ρ gives a nonpositive subharmonic function w_j.

The maxima of u_j are attained. Pass to a subsequence whose maximum points converge to p. In a chart about p, w_j at those points has a uniform lower bound. Submean on fixed-radius balls centred there bounds ∫(−w_j); a fixed smaller ball about p lies in these balls for all sufficiently large j. This supplies an initial uniform L1 bound.

To propagate it, in a connected coordinate domain let S be the points having neighbourhoods with uniformly bounded ∫(−w_j). S is open. If x is in its relative closure, choose B(x,4r) inside the domain and a fixed ball A⊂S∩B(x,r/4). The bound on A supplies points a_j∈A with w_j(a_j)≥−M for one fixed finite M. Submean on B(a_j,r) bounds its integral of −w_j. Since B(x,r/2)⊂B(a_j,r), x∈S. Thus S is relatively closed and equals the connected coordinate domain. Finite coverings then bound every compact subset. Across overlapping charts, bounded corrections and bounded coordinate Jacobians on a smaller overlap transfer these bounds. The intersection graph of a connected finite coordinate cover is connected, so they propagate across the cover. The smaller cores give a global L1 bound. The permitted local psh compactness theorem, followed by finite diagonal extraction, gives local and global L1 convergence. Limits patch as distributions, and uniqueness of canonical psh representatives after smooth correction makes the limit genuine. This proves the required global normalized compactness.

Suppose δ_j→0 and C_{δ_j}≤M. Put κ=1/(M+1). For EVERY smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed test Θ, normalization by ∫ωΘ gives
∫(ω−κB_{δ_j})Θ≥(1−κM)∫ωΘ>0.
Lamari's permitted nonclosed-form criterion yields real distributions u_j with
ω+dd^c u_j≥κB_{δ_j}.
Local quadratic corrections and the permitted representative theorem make these genuine quasi-psh functions. Subtract their finite suprema. Since dd^c u_j≥−ω, the compactness proof applies. Pass to u_j→u in L1.

The ordinary approximate-identity calculation in ζ gives
B_{δ_j}→χ0(x)χ0(y)[D_U],
where D_U={ζ=0} in the product chart; its normalization is ∫pσ_ζ=1. The base cutoffs permit extension by zero. Distributional limits preserve positivity, hence
T=ω+dd^c u≥κχ0(x)χ0(y)[D_U].
Near |x|,|y|<1/2 and ζ=0 this implies T≥κ[D_U].

On each coordinate ball choose ρ=M|z|² with dd^cρ≥ω. The current R=dd^c(u+ρ) is CLOSED and positive and dominates κ[D_U] near that local divisor. Its geometric Lelong number there is at least κ. In the geometric normalization a regular integration-current point has number 1: for a flat complex two-plane, the integral of (σ1+σ2)² over a radius-r ball is r^4. On overlaps the corrected currents differ by a smooth form, whose ball integral is O(r^6) and whose geometric Lelong contribution after division by r^4 is zero. Thus their numbers define one intrinsic function ν_u. Siu applies locally to these closed positive currents of bidimension (2,2). Consequently A={ν_u≥κ/2} is a global closed analytic subset of dimension at most 2 containing the indicated open part of D_U. No Siu theorem for a nonclosed current has been used.

Lift A through the quotient covering to an analytic subset Ã⊂Ω. The hypersurface D0={w0=z0}∩Ω is connected: it is P2 with the two points where z=0 or w=0 removed. Since Ã∩D0 is analytic in that connected surface and contains a nonempty open subset, the identity principle gives D0⊂Ã. Quotient invariance gives Dm={w0=q^m z0}∩Ω⊂Ã for every integer m.

At P=[0:1:0:1]∈Ω use a=z0/z1, b=w0/z1 and r=w1/z1 near (0,0,1). Each Dm is b=q^m a. A local holomorphic defining function F of Ã has expansion F(a,b,r)=Σf_ij(r)a^i b^j. Vanishing on Dm gives, for every degree k and integer m,
Σ_{i+j=k}f_ij(r)q^{mj}=0.
For each r this is a polynomial in q^m with infinitely many distinct roots. All its coefficients vanish. Every f_ij is therefore identically zero. Every local defining function vanishes identically, so Ã has interior near P, contradicting dimension at most 2.

A bounded subsequence of Cδ as δ→0 is impossible; hence Cδ→∞. This proves all of I for every prescribed p and χ0, including finiteness against all tests and the complete concentration implication. No quantitative lower divergence rate is claimed.

notes.summary: Proves II by averaging actual globally embedded rational curves over explicit compact matrix parameters. Tδ,ε are globally smooth semipositive CLOSED forms with uniform ω degree and the required fixed-δ smooth local rank-two limit.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses curves [Z0:Z1]↦[Z0:Z1:e^s(Z0+eZ1):e^s(bZ0+aZ1)], with a near ±1 and e tending to zero. Global submersivity proves smooth fibre integration without an imported regularization theorem. An explicit parameter change yields the coefficient matrix and C∞ convergence on compact subsets for fixed δ. Symmetric slopes and positive densities give B≥cδ^{-2}I2 on Vδ.
notes.text:
Use n1. Let k_R(v) be the smooth probability density relative to σ_v proportional to exp(−1/(1−|v|²/R²)) for |v|<R, zero elsewhere. Then k_R(v)=R^{-2}k_1(v/R). Choose
r(a)=½k_{1/16}(a−1)+½k_{1/16}(a+1),  k(b)=k_1(b).
The density r is symmetric under a↦−a and supported where 7/8≤|a|≤9/8. Reuse any allowed p from I and put pδ(s)=δ^{-2}p(s/δ). Set ε0=1/64, rε=ε0ε/(1+ε)>0 and lε(e)=k_{rε}(e).

For parameters in these supports set M=[[1,e],[b,a]] and define the actual holomorphic curve
F_{a,b,e,s}([Z0:Z1])=[Z0:Z1:e^s(Z0+eZ1):e^s(bZ0+aZ1)]
followed by quotienting to X0. Its determinant a−eb has modulus at least 7/8−1/64>0. Thus neither z nor w vanishes, and the map lands in Ω. The first base projection is the identity of P1, so the quotient curve is embedded.

Define T_{δ,ε} by
∫ξ∧T_{δ,ε}=∫r(a)k(b)pδ(s)lε(e)(∫P1F_{a,b,e,s}^*ξ)σ_aσ_bσ_sσ_e.
All parameter densities are probabilities. Integration over curves proves reality and positivity as a current. Stokes on each compact curve proves dT_{δ,ε}=0.

This current is an ACTUAL globally smooth form. On an open neighbourhood of the compact parameter supports, the incidence map F:P1×parameters→X0 is a holomorphic submersion. At fixed Z, parameter variations span the two complex w-directions: if Z1≠0, variations of e and a do so; if Z1=0, variations of s and b do so. Variation of Z gives the remaining z-base direction. This proves rank 3 everywhere, including infinity and w0=0. The current is the pushforward of the smooth parameter (4,4) form on a complex five-dimensional domain. Submersion coordinates express it as integration of smooth coefficients over the remaining coordinates. A finite partition of unity on the compact support permits differentiation under each integral. It is therefore a globally smooth (2,2) form. Positivity as a smooth current implies pointwise semipositivity. No regularization theorem is assumed.

All matrices M lie in one compact subset of GL2(C), and |s|≤1/100. The maps from P1 times this compact parameter set to X0 have uniformly bounded pullbacks of ω, hence ∫P1F^*ω≤D. More explicitly, the two base contributions are 1+1, while
t∘F=2Re(s)+log(||MZ||²/||Z||²)
has uniformly bounded differential for this compact matrix family. Probability averaging gives ∫ωT_{δ,ε}≤D uniformly in δ and ε.

Fix a compact subset of U_00=C_x×C_y×E_ζ. For sufficiently small ε, 1+ex is uniformly near 1 and has a holomorphic logarithm there. Along a curve,
y=(b+ax)/(1+ex),  ζ=s+log(1+ex) modulo the lattice.
The inverse parameter change is b=(1+ex)y−ax and s=ζ−log(1+ex), with real Jacobian |1+ex|². Let Pδ be the smooth periodic extension of pδ to E. In the specified trace convention,
Q_{δ,ε}=∫r(a)lε(e)k((1+ex)y−ax)Pδ(ζ−log(1+ex))|1+ex|²vv*σ_aσ_e,
where v=(1,(a−ey)/(1+ex),e/(1+ex))^T. Represent H_ξ so that the tangent pullback is (v*H_ξv)σ_x; this fixes the coefficient transpose convention.

For fixed δ, lε is an approximate identity at e=0. The remaining integrand and every derivative in x,y,ζ are uniformly smooth on the fixed compact set. Thus Q_{δ,ε} converges in C∞ to
Q_{δ,0}=Pδ(ζ)∫r(a)k(y−ax)(1,a,0)^T(1,a,0)*σ_a.
Periodicity makes the formulas compatible across logarithmic representatives. They define a locally smooth semipositive T_{δ,0} on the whole product chart. No global extension or convergence uniform in δ is claimed.

On Vδ, |y−ax|≤17/32. Set k*=min_{|b|≤17/32}k(b)>0 and p*=min_{|s|≤1/4}p(s)>0. Symmetry gives
∫r(a)(1,a)^T(1,a)*σ_a=diag(1,∫|a|²r(a)σ_a)≥(7/8)²I2.
Therefore Q_{δ,0}=diag(B,0) on Vδ, with B≥p*k*(7/8)²δ^{-2}I2. This is the requested bound with c independent of δ, and proves every assertion of II.

The construction is retained in artifacts/factor_proof.txt and artifacts/factor_notes.json. Run python artifacts/check_identities.py. Exact auxiliary outputs include det M=a−eb, tangent components (a−ey)/(1+ex) and e/(1+ex), and the parameter Jacobian. These finite checks do not independently verify the global analytic construction.

notes.summary: Proves III by globally averaging witnesses from I and adding the actual closed forms from II. Proves the unique positive square root and obtains diverging root volumes with uniformly bounded ω degree.
notes.detailedSummary: Global affine automorphisms spread each witness's vertical coefficient across Vδ while preserving positivity, dd^c closedness, and uniform degree control. The horizontal block from II supplies a determinant lower bound. Fixed-δ smooth convergence selects actual ε>0 forms. The proof uses all-test divergence only to select witnesses and asserts no restricted-family variational identity.
notes.text:
Use n2 and n3. Put μ=σ_xσ_yσ_ζ. First prove the root assertion. If η has positive Hermitian tangent matrix H, diagonalization and exterior multiplication give Q_{η²}=2det(H)H^{-1} and det Q=8(det H)². Conversely every positive definite Q has the unique positive definite root H=sqrt(det Q/2)Q^{-1}. Hence η³=(3/sqrt(2))sqrt(det Q)μ. These formulas are coordinate invariant, and local roots patch by uniqueness. They are smooth whenever Γ is smooth and strictly positive.

Define a global holomorphic automorphism of X0 by
A_{a,b,s}[z0:z1:w0:w1]=[z0:z1+az0:e^s w0:e^s(w1+bw0)].
It preserves Ω, commutes with g and has a holomorphic inverse. On U_00 it is exactly (x,y,ζ)↦(x+a,y+b,ζ+s). For a normalized strictly positive dd^c-closed Θ define
SδΘ=∫k_2(a)k_2(b)δ^{-2}k_2(s/δ)A_{a,b,s}^*Θ σ_aσ_bσ_s.
This is globally smooth, strictly positive and dd^c-closed. Parameters and inverses lie in one compact automorphism family, so (A^{-1})^*ω≤Kω uniformly. Changing variables gives ∫ωSδΘ≤K∫ωΘ=K.

Let q33 be the ζζ coefficient of Θ, which is nonnegative. Put Kδ={|x|,|y|<1, |ζ|<δ} and Aδ(Θ)=∫BδΘ. Then
Aδ(Θ)≤||p||∞δ^{-2}∫Kδq33μ.
For any point of Vδ, its translation differences to every point of Kδ satisfy |a|,|b|<5/4 and |s|<5δ/4. The averaging kernel there is at least k0δ^{-2} for a fixed k0>0. Translation derivatives are the identity, so
q33(SδΘ)≥k0δ^{-2}∫Kδq33μ≥(k0/||p||∞)Aδ(Θ)
on all of Vδ. This proves an actual trace-concentration estimate.

Choose δ_j=2^{-j}/1000. By n2, C_{δ_j}→∞. Select normalized actual smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed witnesses Θ_j with A_j=∫B_{δ_j}Θ_j≥C_{δ_j}/2 for sufficiently large j. Existence follows from the supremum definition; no maximum is assumed. Let S_j be the matrix of S_{δ_j}Θ_j.

For fixed j the local limit supplied by n3 has horizontal block B≥cδ_j^{-2}I2. Thus the matrix of the local limit of S_{δ_j}Θ_j+T_{δ_j,ε} dominates S_j+d_j diag(1,1,0), where d_j=cδ_j^{-2}. For positive definite S,
det(S+d diag(1,1,0))=det S+d(cof11 S+cof22 S)+d²S33≥d²S33.
The principal minors are nonnegative. Determinant is monotone on positive definite matrices, as is seen by conjugating with the inverse square root of the smaller matrix. Consequently the limit root-volume density on V_{δ_j} is at least
(3/sqrt(2))cδ_j^{-2}sqrt((k0/||p||∞)A_j)μ.

Disk integration gives μ(Vδ)=δ²/4096, so this local limit root volume is at least Lsqrt(A_j) for fixed L>0. Convergence from n3 is smooth on the compact closure of V_{δ_j}, and S_{δ_j}Θ_j is strictly positive there. Choose an actual ε_j>0 small enough that the smooth sum's root-volume integral is at least half that limit. Set Γ_j=S_{δ_j}Θ_j+T_{δ_j,ε_j}. These are globally smooth, strictly positive and dd^c-closed, with ∫ωΓ_j≤K+D and ∫Γ_j^{3/2}≥(L/2)sqrt(A_j)→∞. Their unique smooth positive roots satisfy Γ_j=η_j². This proves III with actual global forms using only fixed-δ convergence.

notes.summary: Completes IV and the named-factor dependency: every smooth Hermitian h on X0 admits genuine sup-normalized smooth strictly positive collapsing potentials, so v_-(h)=0. Original unrestricted P07 closure remains false.
notes.detailedSummary: Smooth Hermitian MA existence with the roots from III gives (h+dd^c u_j)³=c_jη_j³. Smooth Stokes and matrix AM–GM prove ∫(h+dd^c u_j)³≤(∫hΓ_j)³/(∫η_j³)². The numerator is bounded for every fixed arbitrary h and the denominator diverges. This proves all named targets relative to the expressly permitted foundations, without solving the original positive-threshold L1 equation.
notes.text:
Let h be ANY smooth strictly positive Hermitian form on X0. Use Γ_j=η_j² from n4 and set V_j=∫η_j³→∞ and D_j=∫hΓ_j. Compactness gives h≤L_hω for a finite L_h, so 0<D_j≤L_h(K+D) uniformly. No restriction on the metric class is imposed.

Apply the permitted Tosatti–Weinkove smooth existence theorem to X0, h and F_j=log(η_j³/h³). The volume ratio is smooth and strictly positive. The exact hypotheses hold by n1: connected compact smooth X0 has complex dimension 3≥2 and h is Hermitian. The theorem gives smooth source potentials φ_j with sup φ_j=0 and scalars b_j satisfying
(h+i∂bar∂φ_j)³=e^{b_j}η_j³,  h+i∂bar∂φ_j>0.
Set u_j=2πφ_j and c_j=e^{b_j}. Then sup u_j=0 and h_j=h+dd^c u_j>0 satisfies h_j³=c_jη_j³. Existence is the only imported conclusion; the degeneration estimate follows next.

Smooth Stokes gives ∫dd^c u_jΓ_j=∫u_jdd^cΓ_j=0. Explicitly, integration of d(d^c u_j∧Γ_j) gives ∫dd^c u_jΓ_j=∫d^c u_jdΓ_j. Integration of d^c(u_jdΓ_j), using d^c d=−dd^c, gives the second equality. Therefore D_j=∫h_jη_j² without assuming h or η_j closed.

At a point diagonalize h_j relative to η_j, with positive eigenvalues λ1,λ2,λ3. Their product is c_j, and
h_j∧η_j²=((λ1+λ2+λ3)/3)η_j³≥c_j^{1/3}η_j³
by AM–GM. Integration yields D_j≥c_j^{1/3}V_j. Thus
∫X0(h+dd^c u_j)³=c_jV_j≤D_j³/V_j²→0.
This proves the needed inequality directly from smooth Stokes and matrix algebra. No global mass-extrema theorem or restricted-family variational equality is used.

Each u_j is smooth on compact X0, hence bounded, canonical and genuinely h-psh. Each corrected form is strictly positive and has a smooth finite positive Monge–Ampère measure. The specified extended product agrees with the ordinary smooth product here. Since masses of positive bounded h-psh potentials are nonnegative, this sequence proves v_-(h)=0. These are actual smooth strictly positive forms, not formal current limits or t-only tests.

Together n1–n4 prove the quotient geometry and EVERY proposed statement I–III; this note proves IV for EVERY smooth Hermitian h. The complete named-factor theorem is therefore proved in this ordinary unverified draft relative only to the expressly allowed foundations. No false named target or unresolved indispensable premise remains in this reconstruction. Selection of test witnesses and MA solutions is nonconstructive but supplies actual smooth objects. Recursive certification of the allowed foundations' cited dependencies is not claimed.
